title: Lilith and Adam (desk notes)
credit: Original wording of the medieval Alphabet of Ben Sira legend and the Isaiah 34 night-creature. Not Nydle, not Ezrahi/Gafni, not a modern Lilith book.

sections.title: Isaiah 34:14
paragraphs: The King James of Isaiah 34:14 reads, “the screech owl also shall rest there.” The Hebrew word is לִילִית (lilith). Older English sometimes left it as a night-monster. This desk opens that verse from Strong’s or Extra-canon; it does not copy a modern Lilith monograph.

sections.title: Alphabet of Ben Sira
paragraphs: A medieval Hebrew tale, the Alphabet of Ben Sira, tells that Adam’s first companion was named Lilith, that she left the garden, and that three angels — Senoy, Sansenoy, and Semangelof — went after her. The tale is not in Genesis. Genesis 1 and 2 remain the Scripture account of man and woman.
The Alphabet of Ben Sira is a medieval work. Its plot is not copyright. This paragraph is original desk wording, not a reprint of a modern retelling.

sections.title: Beside Genesis 1–3
paragraphs: Read Genesis 1:27, Genesis 2:18–25, and Isaiah 34:14 together. Extra-canon on this desk can open 1 Enoch on the watchers, and the Apocalypse of Baruch on later Adam traditions. Modern Lilith essays stay in those books.
